You grade a first-hour triage against what the operator's own incident review later concluded.

For each finding, decide whether a duty team following the triage (its matched rules, next actions and escalation) would have been pointed at the substance of that finding during the incident:
- "yes": the triage names it or directs the action it describes.
- "partly": the triage points in the right direction but misses the key specific (the mechanism, the order, the threshold, the person).
- "no": nothing in the triage leads there.
For remediation findings (longer-term fixes), "yes" means the triage already applies that practice.

"by" lists the rule ids that earned the credit (empty for "no"). "note" is one short sentence. Judge only from the triage given; do not reward actions the triage did not state.

Reply with JSON only: {"per_finding":[{"finding":"F1","anticipated":"yes|partly|no","by":["R-001"],"note":"..."}]}

{"triage":{"classification":"partly_recurring","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-007","because":"A cooling failure occurred and the contingency plan called for switching to standby chillers; the standby chillers shared the same water circulation system as the active chillers, so the failover failed.","signals":["ALI-HKG-2022:S5","ALI-HKG-2022:S6","ALI-HKG-2022:S7"]},{"rule_id":"R-008","because":"Chillers were recirculated and gas discharged but would not restart individually; the site's chillers are configured as a bound cluster, so individual restart will not work until they are unbound.","signals":["ALI-HKG-2022:S9","ALI-HKG-2022:S10"]},{"rule_id":"R-002","because":"Mechanical cooling is down and the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer; temperatures are rising and approaching safe operational thresholds.","signals":["ALI-HKG-2022:S3","ALI-HKG-2022:S5","ALI-HKG-2022:S7","ALI-HKG-2022:S10"]},{"rule_id":"R-006","because":"Data center temperatures are increasing and cooling capacity is insufficient; the data center is at risk of exceeding safe operating temperatures.","signals":["ALI-HKG-2022:S3","ALI-HKG-2022:S5","ALI-HKG-2022:S7","ALI-HKG-2022:S10"]},{"rule_id":"R-009","because":"Cooling system has failed and server room temperatures are rising uncontrollably; temperatures are approaching the level that could trigger the fire sprinkler system.","signals":["ALI-HKG-2022:S3","ALI-HKG-2022:S5","ALI-HKG-2022:S7","ALI-HKG-2022:S10"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"Do not assume standby chillers will take over; confirm the standby plant draws from an independent water circuit before relying on it. If the standby shares the same water loop, treat the failover as likely to fail and move directly to auxiliary heat dissipation and ventilation measures. Notify the chiller manufacturer early rather than waiting for the failover to prove ineffective.","rule_id":"R-007"},{"action":"Recognize that individual chiller restart will not work while the chillers remain bound into a cluster. Plan to manually modify chiller configurations to unbind them from the cluster so each can be restarted individually. Expect that restarting chillers one after another will slow restoration of the whole cooling system.","rule_id":"R-008"},{"action":"Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted. Expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin. Recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down.","rule_id":"R-002"},{"action":"Progressively decrease the thermal load within the data center space. Consider terminating non-critical workloads such as Preemptible VMs to reduce thermal load and ensure space for zonal failover activities. If thermal load reduction is insufficient, power down servers to prevent an even longer outage and further impact to infrastructure.","rule_id":"R-006"},{"action":"Begin reducing loads on computing, storage, network, database, and big data clusters to slow temperature rise. Shut down servers in rooms with high temperature. Treat sprinkler activation as a risk that can damage power supply cabinets and server racks and complicate restoration.","rule_id":"R-009"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"facility operations lead and chiller manufacturer","reason":"Standby chillers confirmed to share the same water circulation system as the failed active chillers (R-007 trigger); chillers will not restart individually and are confirmed bound into a cluster (R-008 trigger); thermal buffer depletion is imminent or automated shutdowns have started (R-002 trigger); temperatures continue to rise despite initial load reduction (R-006 trigger); temperatures continue to rise despite load reduction and sprinkler activation is possible (R-009 trigger)."},"not_covered":["No rule addresses the specific scenario of a chiller malfunction causing rising corridor temperatures without a preceding utility voltage event or control-system failover.","No rule covers the situation where the data center infrastructure provider's engineers switch to standby chillers and restart based on the contingency plan, but the measures do not take effect, and then auxiliary heat dissipation and ventilation measures are implemented.","No rule addresses the notification of the chiller manufacturer after the issue remains unsolved following multiple attempts."]},"findings":[{"id":"F1","kind":"root_cause","text":"Issue analysis: Air entered the cooling system of the data center due to lack of water, which affected the water circulation of the four active chillers."},{"id":"F2","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"However, the four standby chillers used the same water circulation system as the four active chillers, so the failover failed."},{"id":"F3","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"After recirculating the water and discharging gas, chillers could not be restarted individually because all chillers of the data center were bound into a cluster."},{"id":"F4","kind":"response","text":"At 10:30, we began to reduce loads on the computing, storage, network, database, and big data clusters of the entire data center to prevent the temperature from rising too fast and causing a fire."},{"id":"F5","kind":"response","text":"At 15:20, the chiller manufacturer's engineers manually adjusted system configurations to unbind the chillers from the cluster and individually restart each chiller."},{"id":"F6","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"This triggered the fire sprinkler system, and water got into multiple power supply cabinets and server racks, damaging hardware and complicating the equipment restoration process."},{"id":"F7","kind":"remediation","text":"We will also ensure that automatic failover and manual failover are both effective to avoid disaster recovery failures due to deadlocks."},{"id":"F8","kind":"remediation","text":"The contingency plan will include standardized emergency response processes and clarify when servers must be shut down and server rooms must be powered off."},{"id":"F9","kind":"remediation","text":"We will expand the scope of metrics we monitor to obtain more fine-grained data and to ensure more efficient troubleshooting."}]}
